papers.title: Breaking Up, Holding On: Differentiation of Self as a Mediator in Post-Relationship Pursuit.
papers.abstract: Stalking and unwanted pursuit behaviors following a romantic breakup, referred to as post-relationship pursuit (PRP), pose significant psychological and emotional risks for victims. While research has highlighted elevated rates of stalking victimization among gender and sexual minority (GSM) individuals, little is known about the mechanisms underlying PRP perpetration in this population. This study investigates differentiation of self as a mediating factor between GSM status and PRP perpetration. A sample of 687 young adults (ages 18-24) completed measures of differentiation of self and PRP behaviors. Results revealed that GSM individuals exhibited lower levels of differentiation of self compared to cisgender heterosexual individuals. Mediation analyses indicated that while GSM status was not directly associated with PRP perpetration, it was indirectly related through differentiation of self, suggesting that lower differentiation may contribute to relational intrusions post-breakup. These findings highlight the role of differentiation in managing relational boundaries and emotional regulation, particularly in populations vulnerable to minority stress.

papers.title: The Association Between Victims' Anxious Attachment and Transgressors' Nonapology on Conflict Resolution in Romantic Relationships.
papers.abstract: Relational transgressions are inevitable in romantic relationships. When a partner transgresses against the other partner, a victim's response may be motivated by their attachment style and their partner's post-transgression responses. In the current research, we tested whether victims higher in attachment anxiety would use more destructive responses, and whether this effect differed by romantic partners' nonapologetic response (e.g. lashing out). We also tested whether these associations were accounted for by lower perceived partner availability and responsiveness. Across three studies using correlational and experimental methods, victims high in attachment anxiety reported more destructive responses when they perceived their offending partner as nonapologetic. Study 3 findings showed that this moderated association was not accounted for by lower perceived partner availability and responsiveness. However, Study 3 shows a negative association between victims' attachment anxiety and their perceptions of their partner's availability and responsiveness when their partner does not respond, compared to when their partner responds nonapologetically, which may explain their destructive responses. These findings suggest that offending partners' responses play a role in motivating anxiously attached victims' responses.

papers.title: Immobilization of fungal cells on positively charged cyclodextrin-based carriers: Enhanced PhAC degradation and multi-omics implications.
papers.abstract: The rational design of cellular interfaces is essential for advancing biocatalytic systems. White rot fungi are promising biodegraders of pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs), but they are readily inactivated in wastewater treatment, while conventional carriers cannot simultaneously immobilize cells and retain extracellular enzymes. In this study, a stable fungus-enzyme synergistic interface was constructed by assembling Trametes versicolor with a positively charged porous thienyl cyclodextrin polymer (Th-CDP) to form Tv@Th-CDP. This design simultaneously immobilized fungal cells and retained their secreted laccases within the carrier, enhancing PhAC removal in continuous-flow reactors treating secondary municipal effluent to 93%. The system demonstrated sustained 30-d performance and reduced effluent toxicity by 58%. This performance was associated with the high positive charge density of Th-CDP, which enhanced mycelial attachment and laccase retention (48.2 U kg-1). Furthermore, the hydrophobic cavities of cyclodextrin, coupled with electrostatic interactions, enhanced PhAC adsorption and enriched Trametes sp. (46%). This immobilization strategy improved the fungus-enzyme interactions, with enhanced laccase-related catalytic currents observed in electrochemical assays. Metaproteomics analysis and transformation pathway identification supported a degradation model mediated by electrostatic interactions between the fungus and the retained enzymes. A total of 305 proteins associated with oxidoreductase activity were enriched, while the key enzymes aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) and epoxide hydrolase (EPHX2) were upregulated. These changes coincided with enhanced C-N bond cleavage, indicating activation of associated metabolic pathways. Overall, this study provides mechanistic understanding of immobilization mediated by electrostatic interactions and demonstrates its potential to improve the biodegradation of emerging contaminants in engineered biocatalytic

papers.title: Innovative Violence Prevention Education for Health Professionals: Project ECHO.
papers.journal: Journal of medical education and curricular development
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: In 2024 the Surgeon General declared firearm violence a public health crisis. Suicide by firearm continues to rise despite much public health outreach. Fortunately, health professionals are uniquely positioned to educate their patients on violence prevention and firearm safety. METHODS: The Violence Prevention (VP) ECHO team developed a curriculum based on the most common etiologies: substance use, domestic and intimate partner violence, poor mental health, and social and environmental determinants of health. Thirty-six virtual sessions divided into 5 Series were developed between Fall 2023 and Fall 2025. RESULTS: A total of 1172 unique participants attended 5664 times from 45 US states, and 27 other countries. Most were allied health professionals (34%) followed by social workers (24%), nurses/nurse practitioners (14%) and doctors (6%). A total of 2163 no-cost continuing medical education/education units (CME/CEU) were given. SERIES 1: A retrospective pre-post survey evaluation showed significant improvement in all categories of knowledge and self-efficacy (p<.0001). SERIES 2: A linked virtual poll (N=45) assessing knowledge (etiology of firearm deaths) and self-efficacy (communication skills with patients) demonstrated significant improvement (p<.0001) between sessions 1 and session 8. SERIES 3: Survey results showed that participants significantly improved knowledge and self-efficacy 3-months post-series. SERIES 1-5: The overall response rate for the post-evaluation surveys was 45% and 2163 CME/CEU were awarded. A total of 1,733 (68%) survey respondents reported that they will use what they learned in the sessions while 57% reported that there were no barriers to using what they had learned. CONCLUSIONS: The VP ECHO program can successfully train hundreds of health professionals on firearm violence prevention by improving knowledge, self-efficacy and communication skills. papers.title: "Through their eyes": Narratives of resilience among adolescents exposed to intimate partner violence in early childhood.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood exposure to intimate partner violence (CEIPV) is a serious form of developmental trauma with lasting effects on emotional regulation, relational functioning, and identity formation. While much research emphasizes risk and pathology, less is known about how adolescents interpret these early experiences and construct resilience. OBJECTIVE: To explore how adolescents exposed to IPV in early childhood make sense of their experiences and articulate resilience through personal narratives. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Twenty-one adolescents (aged 13-18) residing in the Abha region of Saudi Arabia participated. All had documented or self-reported exposure to IPV before age 10 and were engaged in community-based psychosocial or youth programs. METHODS: A descriptive phenomenological design guided in-depth, semi-structured interviews. Colaizzi's seven-step method was used for thematic analysis. Interviews were conducted in Arabic, transcribed, translated, and validated through member checking and peer debriefing. RESULTS: Four major themes emerged: (1) Remembering Through Fragments, trauma stored somatically rather than narratively; (2) Becoming My Own Safe Space, emotional self-reliance and boundary setting; (3) Telling My Story, Taking My Power, voice as healing and advocacy; and (4) Resilience Rooted in Connection, relationships, culture, and faith as protective factors. Storytelling facilitated both individual transformation and a desire for peer support and change-making. CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents are not passive witnesses to IPV but meaning-makers and emerging advocates. Trauma-informed, culturally grounded interventions should center youth voice and foster relational, narrative, and spiritual pathways to healing. papers.title: Evolving landscape of depression among 10-24-year-olds in G20 countries from 1990 to 2035: epidemiological trends, modifiable risk factors, drivers of change, and forecasts.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated temporal trends in depression burden among 10-24-year-olds in G20 countries during 1990-2023, identified key risk factors and disparities, quantified drivers of change, and projected trends to 2035. METHODS: Using GBD 2023 data, we analyzed age-standardized incidence (ASIR), prevalence (ASPR), and disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates (ASDR) for depression. Temporal trends were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC). Burden attributable to bullying victimization (BV), childhood sexual abuse (CSA), and intimate partner violence (IPV) was quantified. Decomposition analysis partitioned changes into population growth, aging, and epidemiological components. Exponential smoothing models forecasted burden. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, G20 countries experienced significant increases in depression burden: ASIR rose from 3069.65 to 3441.15 per 100,000 (EAPC = 0.81%, 95% CI: 0.53%-1.08%); ASPR increased from 2935.88 to 3646.70 per 100,000 (EAPC = 0.55%, 95% CI: 0.43%-0.68%); and ASDR rose from 487.44 to 630.35 per 100,000 (EAPC = 0.68%, 95% CI: 0.53%-0.84%). Females bore 1.8 times the burden of males, with the 10-14-year age group demonstrating the most pronounced growth. BV, CSA, and IPV contributed substantially to DALYs (up to 12.4%, 10.2%, and 10.0% respectively). Epidemiological change was the dominant driver in G20 countries (contributing 61.4% to prevalence increases), while population growth predominated in China. Projections indicate continued increases through 2035 with persistent sex disparities. CONCLUSIONS: Depression burden among adolescents and young adults in G20 countries has increased substantially and is projected to rise further. Females and early adolescents are disproportionately affected, and modifiable risk factors contribute significantly. Targeted, developmentally appropriate prevention strategies are urgently needed.

papers.title: Diurnal Cortisol Covaries with Observer-Rated but Not Self-Reported Professional Relationship Quality: A Four-Wave Within-Person Study.
papers.abstract: Stress impairs prefrontal-dependent behavioral control and shifts processing toward automatic defaults, but whether this extends to the quality of real-world professional relationships, where skilled interpersonal engagement is itself a predictor of client outcomes, is unknown. In a four-wave longitudinal study of 46 community supervision officers, we tested whether diurnal cortisol predicted relationship quality assessed by independent observers from 2,126 video-recorded sessions (732 supervisees) and by officers themselves via survey (432 supervisees). Two-level models with latent mean centering identified two within-person effects implicating different cortisol indices and different relational dimensions: higher total cortisol output (log AUCg) predicted lower observer-rated Caring/Fairness, and flatter diurnal slope predicted lower observer-rated Trust. These effects were independent, robust across sensitivity specifications, and specific, with neither index predicting the other's target. The slope effect reflected the trajectory of diurnal decline rather than evening or waking level alone. No cortisol index predicted officer-reported relationship quality, consistent with both the controlled-to-automatic framework and the trait-like variance structure of officer self-report (63-73% between-person). The findings suggest that HPA dysregulation covaries with what independent observers see in professional relational behavior but not with what the professional perceives. That distinct cortisol indices reached distinct relational dimensions is consistent with separable biological pathways rather than a general stress-to-relationship process.
